It also only covered the moratorium's removal, not the bill becoming law. e2's public excerpt is just "4", a fragment of "July 4" that conveys nothing on its own, so the citation is misstated. e1's "99–1" is minimal but acceptable.

The excerpt is unaltered and the proposition is faithful. The interpretation notes that the trends proviso is only context. The rationale correctly reads e1 as national convergence that fits the forecast without settling parity between firms or that profit is the only difference. Outcome unresolved and horizon open match the reviews. e1's excerpt, publisher, March 2026 date and context relation are correct. "Strongest cited comparison" is slightly odd with one item but not an overclaim.
